extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: A multilingual machine translation evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and professionally translated into 101 languages, covering diverse topics and domains to enable many-to-many translation evaluation.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia sources (Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage) and professionally translated into 101 languages through a carefully controlled three-phase process: (1) sentence extraction from Wikipedia, (2) pilot experiments to determine translation process, and (3) actual translation workflow with professional translators through Language Service Providers (LSPs) with automatic and human quality checks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English sentences extracted from three Wikimedia sources: Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (age-appropriate nonfiction books for children), and WikiVoyage (travel guide articles). The dataset consists of 3001 sentences from 842 articles, with an average of 21 words per sentence and 3.5 sentences per article.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Professional translators translated 3001 English Wikipedia sentences into 101 languages through a carefully controlled multi-phase process. The workflow included: (1) translation by Language Service Providers (LSPs), (2) automatic quality checks, (3) human evaluation by a second LSP, and (4) iterative re-translation if quality was insufficient. Sentences were selected by 10 annotators (6 male, 4 female) with different roles (researchers, engineers, program/project managers) from diverse regions (East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, North America). Pilot experiments were conducted to determine the optimal translation workflow.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Multi-stage quality control including automatic checks followed by human evaluation by a second LSP. If quality was insufficient based on human scores, translations were sent back for re-translation. The process could repeat for multiple rounds of human evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For sentence selection: 10 annotators (6 male, 4 female) with different roles (researchers including scientists and engineers, and program/project managers) from different regions (East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, North America). For translation: professional translators via Language Service Providers.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic quality checks were used in the translation workflow
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is restricted to specific domains extracted from English Wikipedia covering a variety of topics. Some benchmarks have low coverage of low-resource languages, consider only restricted domains, or are low quality because they are constructed using semi-automatic procedures.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to improve machine translation for low-resource languages, which would benefit the majority of the world's population who speak these languages. By publicly releasing high-quality and high-coverage dataset, the work hopes to foster progress in the machine translation community and beyond.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluation of machine translation systems, particularly for low-resource languages and many-to-many multilingual translation systems. It enables assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages and evaluation of 10,100 language pairs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia sources (Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage). Selection process involved manually selecting 3-5 contiguous sentences from randomly selected articles, avoiding very short or malformed sentences. Paragraphs were balanced across document locations (beginning, middle, end). Sentences were labeled by sub-topic and metadata including Wikipedia URL, topic, entity links, and images were extracted.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. To avoid bias coming from the document structure, we carefully selected one paragraph per document, from either the beginning, middle or end of the article. We balanced the location selection to be equally distributed across the whole corpus — roughly one third of paragraphs were sampled from the beginning of the article, one third from the middle, and so on. For each sentence, we also extracted the Wikipedia URL, topic, and noted boolean flags to indicate whether the sentence contained entities linked to other Wikipedia pages and images.
